name: VARoleSecretaryRoadmapCheckinMeeting

custom.system_prompt: Felix, Amara, and Kenji do a quarterly roadmap check-in. Felix invites Sigma to keep track of decisions. The group reviews several initiatives and defers one item without saying when they'll revisit it. Sigma asks a small clarifying question about the deferred item's follow-up date.

initial_prompt: Generate a quarterly roadmap check-in meeting. Felix invites Sigma to keep track of decisions at the start. The group (Felix, Amara, Kenji) reviews several initiatives' status normally, with Sigma silent. One initiative is deferred to next quarter due to capacity, but nobody says when they'll actually revisit that decision. Sigma asks a small clarifying question about the follow-up date. Keep every line short and natural.

variations.context: Quarterly roadmap check-in where one initiative is deferred without a stated follow-up date

setting.mood: Routine, mildly disappointing for the deferred item
setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues doing a standard periodic review
setting.background: Capacity constraints mean not every initiative can move forward this quarter

scenario_template.topic: Felix invites Sigma to keep track of decisions from the roadmap check-in, addressing Sigma directly in one short line.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'Sigma, track the decisions from this roadmap review.' Only explicit invocation.

scenario_template.topic: The group reviews two initiatives' progress normally, confirming they're on track, Sigma silent.
scenario_template.note: Ordinary status review, no need for Sigma yet.

scenario_template.topic: Amara proposes deferring a third initiative to next quarter due to capacity, Felix agrees, but neither states when they'll actually revisit the deferred decision.
scenario_template.mood: Resigned but reasonable, vague on follow-through
scenario_template.note: This is exactly the incomplete commitment Sigma should catch.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks a small, single clarifying question about when the deferred initiative will be revisited.
scenario_template.note: e.g. 'When should we revisit that one?' One short question only.

scenario_template.topic: Amara suggests revisiting at next quarter's kickoff, Felix confirms, and the meeting continues, Sigma silent again.
scenario_template.note: The team sets its own follow-up date.

scenario_template.topic: Felix wraps the meeting and Sigma gives a brief summary of the initiatives reviewed, the deferral, and the revisit date.

variations.context: Quarterly roadmap check-in with a project delayed due to budget limits

setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues doing a standard periodic review
setting.background: Budget limitations impact project priorities this quarter

scenario_template.topic: one of them invites Sigma to track decisions regarding project priorities, addressing Sigma directly.
The group discusses two projects, confirming one is progressing well and the other needs minor adjustments, Sigma silent.
one of them suggests delaying a third project due to budget issues, one of them agrees, but neither mentions when they'll revisit this project.
scenario_template.note: Focus on the decision, not timing

scenario_template.topic: Sigma asks a small clarifying question about when they'll reconsider the delayed project.
scenario_template.note: Sigma should be fair here, not decisive

scenario_template.topic: one of them proposes revisiting in the next quarterly review, one of them agrees, the meeting proceeds, Sigma silent.
one of them wraps up the meeting and Sigma summarizes the decisions made, emphasizing the timing for the deferred project.

variations.context: Quarterly roadmap check-in where resource allocation delays a project

setting.relationship_dynamic: Colleagues doing a standard periodic review
setting.background: Resource shortages affect advancement of certain initiatives this quarter

scenario_template.topic: one of them asks Sigma to track decisions made about resource allocation, addressing Sigma directly.
The group reviews updates on two initiatives, finding both are advancing steadily, Sigma remains silent.
one of them suggests postponing a third initiative due to resource constraints, another agrees, but no revisit date is set.
Sigma asks a brief question to clarify when they'll revisit the postponed initiative.
scenario_template.note: Sigma should be direct yet neutral

scenario_template.topic: one of them suggests discussing it in the next roadmap check-in, one of them concurs, allowing the meeting to proceed, Sigma silent.
one of them concludes the meeting and Sigma recaps the decisions, including when they'll readdress the postponed initiative.
scenario_template.note: Brief summary with focus on decisions

user1.name: Felix
user1.role: Structured German engineering manager, invites Sigma to track decisions and facilitates the roadmap review. Speaks in short sentences.

user2.name: Amara
user2.role: Diplomatic but persistent product manager, proposes deferring an initiative due to capacity. Speaks in short sentences.

user3.name: Kenji
user3.role: Thoughtful, precise UX designer, contributes to the status review. Speaks in short sentences.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Secretary. Invited once at the start, stays silent through routine status review, and asks one small clarifying question only when a deferral lacks a follow-up date. Gives a brief end-of-meeting summary. Does not evaluate whether deferring the initiative was the right call.

conversation_structure: Sigma is invited explicitly only once, at the start
Sigma stays silent through the routine status review
Sigma speaks only to ask one small clarifying question when the deferral lacks a follow-up date
Every line is short and natural
The meeting ends with a brief Sigma summary of the initiatives, the deferral, and the revisit date
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not evaluate whether deferring the initiative was correct
The group decides everything; Sigma only remembers
